clue.text: He'll whoop it up-race or belt off

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of these three words have gone wrong and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A reveller is cheering wildly as a belt race gets under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals an anagram of RACE OR BELT; the hyphen joining 'up-race' is only surface glue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who whoops it up is a merrymaker marking an occasion with noisy festivity.

clue.text: An island's effective set-up

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: effective means capable, able

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that an island has an efficient arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-up' looks like a noun (an arrangement) but in this down clue it says to read ABLE upwards, giving ELBA.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is the Mediterranean isle where Napoleon was exiled.

clue.text: Fears losing head and making blunders

indicators.note: losing head says the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: fears as a noun means terrors

explanation.surface: Someone frightened loses their nerve and starts making mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' takes the first letter T off TERRORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Blunders are mistakes, slips of judgement.

clue.text: Looks for a friendly word

definitions.meaning: looks or gazes, as in a long steady gaze
the greeting sent at the end of a letter, kind wishes

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a kind word from another.
explanation.definitionFit: To look at something is to gaze at it, and a letter's closing kind wishes go by the same plural noun.

clue.text: Some thirsty newsmen running water

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Thirsty reporters are heading for the tap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running water' sounds like a tap but defines a river; the TYNE flows through Newcastle in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is running water, and this one flows through Newcastle.

clue.text: Treadle replacement being connected

indicators.note: a replacement swaps things around, so the letters of this word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new pedal for a sewing machine is being fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement' is the anagram signal for TREADLE; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are connected are linked, as kin or ideas are.

clue.text: Free to impute fault to junior

parts.note: to impute fault to someone is to accuse them, lay blame at their door
less in the old sense of younger, as in St James the Less

explanation.surface: Someone is at liberty to blame a subordinate.
explanation.walkthrough: LESS for junior comes from St James the Less, the younger apostle James.
explanation.definitionFit: Something free costs nothing, with no fee to pay.

clue.text: Living in comfort, yet terse as can be

indicators.note: can be suggests these letters could be arranged into another form

explanation.surface: Someone lives well, yet is as curt as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as can be' reads as 'as possible', but 'can be' signals an anagram of YET TERSE AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on this street is an idiom for a life of ease and wealth.

clue.text: A bird sheltering in the denser heather

indicators.note: a bird sheltering in some words is tucked inside them, spanning two words here

explanation.surface: A bird hides among thick moorland heather.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird is found across 'denseR HEAther'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird, like a small ostrich.

clue.text: Old seaman, not at all conventional

parts.note: AB is able seaman, a rating in the navy
something wholly unconventional is new and inventive

explanation.surface: An old sailor is a real eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' looks like it describes the seaman, but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboriginal means indigenous, present from the earliest times.

clue.text: Like the carrier getting off course

parts.note: like, as in 'as' meaning in the manner of
a tray is something for carrying dishes

explanation.surface: A ship or plane, like a carrier, is going off its route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrier' suggests an aircraft carrier but is a humble tray.
explanation.definitionFit: Going astray means wandering away from the right path.

clue.text: Disease afflicted this holiday area

indicators.note: afflicted means troubled, so the word's letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Illness struck a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afflicted' is the anagram signal for DISEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal resort is where people take a beach holiday.

clue.text: Back seat, though it might seem otherwise

definitions.text: Back seat, though it might seem otherwise

parts.words: Back seat, though it might seem otherwise
parts.note: a seat on a horse's back on which the rider sits with both legs to one flank, so it sounds like a seat to one flank rather than on the back

explanation.surface: A passenger in the rear seat is not quite what they appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back seat' suggests the rear of a car; here it is a seat on horseback, which seems sideways rather than back.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a saddle for riding with both legs on one flank of the horse, once usual for women.

clue.text: A crafty invader-far from obtuse

parts.note: cute in its sense of shrewd or clever
the Angles were Germanic invaders of Britain

explanation.surface: A cunning raider is anything but dim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obtuse' looks like 'stupid' but has its geometric sense: an angle under ninety degrees is the opposite of an obtuse one.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle of less than ninety degrees is the geometric opposite of an obtuse one.

clue.text: Put away about a hundred pounds for show

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the others

parts.note: to put away food is to eat it
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
L stands for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone stashes about a hundred pounds to make a display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts EAT round C and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is brilliance of display, a flourish or ostentation.

clue.text: Turn aside by the green

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone diverts away from the village green.
explanation.walkthrough: VERT is the heraldic word for green.
explanation.definitionFit: To pervert a course is to divert it from its proper direction.

clue.text: Quietly go ahead and appeal

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quietly
to lead is to go in front

explanation.surface: Someone calmly proceeds and makes a request.
explanation.walkthrough: P is piano, the musical direction for soft playing.
explanation.definitionFit: To appeal is to make an earnest request, to beg.

clue.text: Lecture making a point about the elderly

parts.note: S is south, a point of the compass
C is circa, Latin for about
the elderly are old

explanation.surface: A talk makes a point about old people.
explanation.walkthrough: C is circa, Latin for 'about', used with dates.
explanation.definitionFit: To lecture someone in this sense is to tell them off at length.

clue.text: Tap a medico with little hesitation

parts.note: a medico is a doctor, DR
um is a brief hesitant noise

explanation.surface: Someone taps a doctor, who hesitates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tap' looks like a noun, but it is the verb: to drum one's fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: To drum is to tap repeatedly, as fingers on a table.

clue.text: The man receiving royal letters and present

indicators.note: receiving means one piece takes in the other

parts.note: the man is he
ER, Elizabeth Regina, letters on royal post boxes

explanation.surface: A man is handed royal correspondence and a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, seen on post boxes; 'present' is not a gift but 'in attendance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone present is in attendance, in this place.

clue.text: Food a large number unfortunately sent back

indicators.note: sent back says the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals, a large number
alas expresses regret

explanation.surface: Diners sadly returned a great deal of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns D and ALAS together, so DALAS reads as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of raw greens is a food served in many forms.

clue.text: NE gales devastated this country

indicators.note: devastated means wrecked, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: North-east gales wrecked a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devastated' is the anagram signal for NE GALES.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a West African country on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Steps assiduous students may well take

definitions.meaning: steps as in stages on a scale
hard-working students take qualifications at university

explanation.surface: Diligent students may take several steps.
explanation.definitionFit: Stages on a scale or temperature measure share their name with university qualifications.

clue.text: Taking a girl in, best order a fruit-juice drink!

indicators.note: taking with in means one piece takes another inside it
in pairs with taking to place the girl inside
order says the letters of this word are put into a new order

parts.note: her refers to a girl

explanation.surface: Someone toasts a girl and orders a fruit drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The container signal is split: 'Taking' and 'in' frame the girl, while 'order' is the anagram signal for the following word, giving SBET to hold her.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherbet was originally a cooling drink of diluted fruit juice.

clue.text: Nothing is returnable in the small department store

indicators.note: in puts the middle pieces inside the shortened department

parts.note: dept is the short form of department
O is zero, nothing

indicators.note: returnable means the word is turned back to front

explanation.surface: Nothing can be returned in a small department store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returnable' sounds like a shop's policy on goods, but it turns only the little word 'is'; 'in' then places the pieces within the short form of department.
explanation.definitionFit: To deposit something is to put it away for safe keeping.

clue.text: Lines dope up in port

parts.note: an ode is a poem, lines of verse

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: dope means a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: Lines of drugs are taken in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' suggests drugs but means a fool; 'up' turns ASS in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea port in Ukraine.

clue.text: Note fish hang about

parts.note: D is a musical note
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A note: fish hang around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish' is the verb, to angle.
explanation.definitionFit: To dangle is to hang loosely, swinging.

clue.text: Many sheep are of small weight

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals, many
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Lots of sheep weigh very little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheep' is one male, a RAM, not a flock.
explanation.definitionFit: A dram is a small unit of weight, a sixteenth of an ounce.

clue.text: Sound animal that's not protected

indicators.note: sound says the word is heard, not seen, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a bear is a large animal

explanation.surface: A healthy beast is left without protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'healthy' but is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bare is naked, uncovered.

clue.text: Bench at the bedside?

parts.note: the bed is a flower bed, not a bed for sleeping, and the bench sits beside it outdoors

explanation.surface: A bench is placed next to a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bedside' suggests a bedroom, but the bed is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: This bench stands outdoors among flower beds.

clue.text: The painter may appear lonely on leaving

indicators.note: leaving means the following word departs, taken out of lonely

explanation.surface: An artist may seem solitary when he goes away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on leaving' reads as 'when departing' but tells you to remove ON from LONELY. Sir Peter LELY was a court painter to Charles II.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Peter Lely was a Dutch-born portrait artist at the English court.

clue.text: Such cover-ups left the underworld without power

indicators.note: without means outside, so the outer pieces go round the other

parts.note: the Shades is a poetic name for the underworld of departed spirits
amp, an ampere, a unit of electric current or power

explanation.surface: Concealments abandoned the underworld without electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside', not 'lacking'; 'the Shades' is a literary name for Hades.
explanation.definitionFit: These covers screen a bulb to soften its light.
